title: Enjoying Elderberries
source_topic: ICPC / The 2018 Asia Hanoi Regional Contest
statement: A rooted tree's internal nodes are big or small; every leaf holds a labelled giant bird, tiny bird or berry. A tiny bird controls its parent's subtree, a giant bird its nearest big ancestor's, and the smallest controlling bird of matching label eats a berry. With every tiny bird turned giant and at most seven birds per label, the fewest labels must change so no berry changes eater.
